purpose: Ordinary existing write latency attribution; no new browser/timing runs
units: milliseconds except explicit traceMicroseconds; counts are integers

method.sampleId: stage/count/variant/repetition/writeIndex plus exact animationId; captureIndex indexes ordinary latency.presentations and captures
method.clock: Start trace clock is exact identified presentation ts minus recorded sample.milliseconds; parse/render boundary endpoints validated against ordinary presentation record within 0.05ms. Source measure b/e pairs retain name+pid+tid+id2 identity. Each renderer frame is contained in AnimationFrame with exact presentation animationId.
method.split: writeToParseEnd + parseEndToRenderBegin + renderToBoundaryEnd + boundaryEndToAck = latency (validated to 0.05ms). Inclusive packing/upload/submit union components explain renderToBoundaryEnd; residual is other renderer work. Medians of components do not add to the latency median.
method.packing: Before ghostty JS rebuildRows; after ZigFrameBuilder.build includes JS options packing plus synchronous WASM native bridge; native-only call is not instrumented. xterm _updateModel is an equivalent model-work control, not the same instance producer.
method.scheduling: previousBoundaryToWrite uses nearest preceding main-thread AnimationFrame::Render b; requestToFire matches exact callback ID containing chosen draw; earlier draws count terminal 0 only; xterm submissions are individual drawElementsInstanced calls, not frame count.
method.quantiles: p50 middle-two average, p95 nearest rank; pooled = all 384 writes, headline = median of four per-run p50s. Representatives nearest per-run p50. Presentation ACK is on-demand headless-shell, not physical vsync.
method.zeroDurationSpans: Zero-duration performance measures are Chrome ph=n events with args.startTime; counted once with start=end. Positive duration measures pair ph=b/e using name+pid+tid+id2.
method.phase: previousBoundaryElapsedModuloRefreshPeriod is elapsed since preceding observed AnimationFrame::Render modulo per-run measured refreshPeriod. It describes sampling-phase mixture approximately; idle frames without callbacks are absent, and boundary timestamp jitter prevents a precise physical-vsync phase claim.
method.headlineDecomposition: Sort runs by write p50, select central two runs; each run p50 is central two latency-ordered original samples. Average those four sample splits. Unlike component medians, these additive components exactly explain the headline p50 statistic (trace/performance alignment error <0.05ms per sample). clockAlignmentResidual exposes sub-0.05ms Chrome performance/trace timestamp alignment differences, making the selected-cohort additive total exact.

limitations: Ordinary samples are not time-paired before/after; separate sessions can have different sample phase mixtures.

Write batch sequentially awaits screencast colored glyph before launching next sample; captures prove glyph correctness while endpoint is Chrome presentation identity. Sampling phase can move as ACK/capture/driver scheduling changes.
Comparison traces serialize source measures after sampling; span timestamp positions reflect recorded historical performance timestamps.

Native build status/result, missing-glyph registration itself, producer full flag and changed range counts are not directly recorded. Multiple build calls/rebuildRows/no-submit frames provide route evidence but cannot identify every internal condition.
No native-only timing span; build inclusive duration must not be described as exclusively native CPU.
No physical display-vsync/GPU execution claim from these headless-shell hardware traces.
A separately found rolling-output full-scroll/full-upload issue is not inferred to explain these no-scroll write-marker samples. This artifact contains frozen V1 before/initial-after treatment only.

diagnosis.status: No confirmed change-related fixable production bug in ordinary writes
diagnosis.mechanism: One-terminal headline shift is pre-render rAF waiting in the central sample cohort, not added packing or submission work. At 17 terminals the central cohort includes both rAF wait and submit-to-ACK increase; unchanged xterm shifts by almost the same overall headline amount. Run and batch phase mixtures vary; these traces do not establish a causal renderer scheduling regression.
diagnosis.knownGoodObservability: Before ordinary traces contain rebuildRows/upload/submit and exact matching Presentation IDs; after traces contain build/uploadFrame/submit and exact IDs. Source spans and identities validated in every analyzed write.

sourceInterpretation.fact: Both paths enter the same scheduled drawFrame. Zig calls build; status 2 causes a second build after glyph registration; fallback reaches rebuildRows. Successful measured after writes show only one build and one submit.
schedule requests one callback, runFrame clears pending handle then calls renderer; unchanged by this production change.
build span includes JavaScript argument/options packing and bridge.buildFrame; no native-only span is available.
write start is timestamped before direct writeMarker; ordinary delayFrames=0.
Writes run sequentially after awaiting the colored-glyph screencast capture. This couples sample launch phase to capture/driver timing.
Endpoint uses exact containing AnimationFrame identity and matching Chrome presentation; PNG capture time is not the endpoint.

scrollPathway.scope: Measured ordinary write-marker samples only; no rolling-output byte probe
scrollPathway.payload: Cursor home + color + eight # + reset (bench/comparison-fixtures.ts:77–78), no LF or wrap at 40 columns.
scrollPathway.source: session.ts:1454–1460 writeNow calls emitScrollChange; 1590–1594 only emits if scrollbackLength/viewportActive/scrollbar fields change; equality at 928–935 excludes cursor position. Terminal.handleScroll (1096–1100) is therefore not expected for the repeated no-scroll marker payload.
scrollPathway.limitation: notifyScroll calls, native full option and uploaded byte lengths were not directly recorded in ordinary latency source spans; an exact runtime zero-scroll claim cannot be proved from these events alone. All after marker samples do show one native build and one submitted frame, with shorter build/render work than baseline.

sourceEvidenceReadingPhase: Hashes describe source read during V1 investigation, not a new timing treatment. Raw comparison manifest source/bundle hashes identify the frozen before and initial-after measurements. A separate rolling-output scroll fix is outside this latency artifact.

verification.assertions: Exact representative ACK identities, containing animation frames, source sequences, sample counts, additive splits and route/frame invariants pass; xterm model work is a snapshot span.
